resolutions: No — delegation already runs workspace-write via the companion's hardcoded --write mapping; the flip closes the dormant default for every OTHER Codex session against the repo config. The decision record states this honestly; per-task escalation plumbing is deferred pending a companion sandbox flag.

Hooks.json is frozen gate surface (0038's fail-closed hooks) — drift must fail integrity. Config.toml must stay editable because the deliberate, diff-visible edit IS the escape hatch; hashing it would force clients needing broader access to break the integrity gate.

Visibility, not prevention, by design: the edit appears in the client's diff and history, the decision record names the expectation, and the vendored default returns on every upgrade — same drift-defense ceiling as 0030, not an adversarial sandbox.

The suite proves the vendored artifacts and integrity mechanics; the live workspace-write proof is the story's own real delegation run, recorded in the testing artifact — the same live-evidence pattern ROLE2-C4 used.
